facts.text: Residents complete census forms as the country counts its population for a new decade.
The presidential election remains undecided for weeks while disputed ballots are reviewed.
News reports describe the last major concerns about computer dates changing to the new millennium.
Families discuss a closely watched national debate over the accuracy of vote counting.
Air travel changes sharply after attacks on major American landmarks in September.
Airline passengers face tighter security checks before boarding flights.
Mail recipients hear warnings about suspicious envelopes after dangerous letters appear in the news.
Many towns hold candlelight gatherings to remember people lost in the September attacks.
Winter sports competitions in the western United States draw national television audiences.
New federal airport screening procedures become a familiar part of holiday travel.
A widespread summer power outage leaves parts of the northeastern country without electricity.
Families watch reports about a major space shuttle accident during its return to Earth.
National news follows the beginning of a new war in the Middle East.
Robotic explorers send new pictures from the surface of Mars.
A powerful ocean earthquake sends destructive waves across parts of southern Asia.
The presidential election brings long lines to some polling places.
A major hurricane floods neighborhoods along the Gulf Coast and forces families to evacuate.
Communities organize clothing and supply donations for families displaced by coastal storms.
News reports describe the opening of a new national memorial honoring the second world war.
Astronomers announce a new classification that removes one distant world from the list of major planets.
Residents follow reports about a strong earthquake that damages communities in the Pacific.
A major highway bridge collapse prompts discussions about inspections and aging public infrastructure.
Falling house prices make national headlines as more homeowners struggle with mortgage payments.
Large financial institutions fail or seek emergency support during a deepening economic crisis.
The presidential election and inauguration draw unusually large crowds and television audiences.
A new strain of influenza prompts schools and families to review handwashing and illness precautions.
Many television viewers prepare for the nationwide switch from analog to digital broadcasts.
